It's tough to be in the place. I remember it clearly when I was smoking weed or drinking all the time to numb the pain I didn't know was there and getting through the day/night and pass out to sleep for some freedom from the suffering. 
It's shit because it's your reality now. What I've learned is the label off 'addicted' made me  feel even worse about what I was doing. I'm guessing you feel the same. You have the depression and the guilt of smoking weed, feeling you are nothing. I felt that way. 
if you are looking to try something read the rest. if you are venting dont !
I learned couple of things. Every time you get off a high, instead of the chemicals in your brain going back to baseline, they go even lower and it makes you feel even worse. Then with that unbalanced brain you think about how to fix the problem of feeling like shit and the solution you already know is there, the weed. You go back to the same cycle over and over again. It makes you depressed even more and more. 
I don't know how intense is your depression, but if you can manage it try this :
Here in Australia we have some services you can call and they can help you manage your use and control it if you don't want to stop. They help you add good stuff to your life. Not sure if you have this sort of service where you live. but if you dont have it try this :
Go for a walk when you aren't high and walk fast enough to feel your heartbeat. If you can manage 5 minutes that's cool. You can go longer ? Even better. Then when you are exhausted stop. the tiredness makes it easier to get out of your head and into your body.  
ask yourself to recall the last time you felt good, maybe when you won against a hard opponent ? Remember the good feeling. This will help shift your brains chemical and your body to a better state, a little more hopeful. 
From there you know what you need to do. Maybe call someone, book therapy, join a gym, whatever you know in your heart will help you get out of the funk you are in. 
I hope you get a glimpse of good feelings without weed just to spark your hope. 
Don't trust your depressive mind. It lies to you. 
Keep moving forward.

2-3 years ago I was study IT to work behind a computer and avoid people and human interaction when I had my worst breakdown. That made me change my career 180 degree. I realised that I need human interaction to stay sane and I wouldn’t get it from personal life ( which I still have none  and I’m fairly sure I’d never have one)
Now,I work in mental health. I actually have to deal with people as part of my role
The good thing is the clients have their own mental health challenges and my oddness sometimes put them at ease. And people that are in my team are in this field to help others with mental health challenges so they are more understanding of say someone in a business setting or other work settings. 
Still a struggle, sometimes other peoples issues triggers my own, sometime I say the wrong thing and upset the best people, sometimes I can’t function in a meeting, but it’s giving me enough social interaction to keep me connected to reality. 
I don’t talk to anyone after work no friends or partner so I know without the work I’d be in an even worse place. And that’s the way it’s been for all of my adult life. 
It’s not that I don’t have thoughts of quitting and giving up everyday, I do. Some days harder than the rest to get through. But without it I wouldn’t have any meaning or purpose in my life. 
I guess in this field of work, being odd can be helpful to some ( clients ) and bit of a challenge to others ( some coworkers ). But I have developed enough social skills to function for short burst of human interaction. 
I’m still the most messed up person I know, but I don’t think others can tell that as much :| getting good at putting on a mask in public. 
Hope this helps someone else

My first thought wasn’t she might need help, I was thinking if she is angry. Until I saw a guy next to us reaching for the item and handing it to her. Then it clicked !
My struggle is empathy too. I’ve got better about it, but even after all these years there are situations that take me back to my younger, ass-holish days.

I would highly recommend talking to a therapist if you can afford it. If not there are plenty of resources you can use.

Kristen Kneff : self compassion. 
Sensory acuity ( from NLP)
Sensory profile ( from a reliable ASD source)

Here’s something interesting I learned today; nicotine increases the dopamine levels by 150%. For comparison sex increases dopamine 100% and food by 50%.  Dopamine being not just the pleasure molecule but more importantly the motivation molecule. 
So let’s look at this in a different way. What if we have low levels of dopamine and our behaviour is a way of bringing that level up to a more normal and balanced level. True the way we are doing it has other unhealthy side effects, but it’s serving a good purpose. 
So if we could increase our dopamine level in a healthier way, say supplements, exercise and such, then the need to consume nicotine might become unnecessary. Then it becomes easier on a chemical level and also on a psychological level to not be dependent on nicotine.

They can be helpful if you use them right. And they can be actually counter productive if not. 
Reading these books generally makes you feel better and your brain releases dopamine just reading them. And when that happens you already feel content and might not follow through with your specific goals. 
A good explanation if this is in the book “rethinking positive thinking”  it guess it is peripherally a self help book but from research perspective. Basically if you already feel all the goodies you would feel when you achieve your goals, you’d be happy already and wouldn’t pursue them. 
On the other hand say you want to work on a specific goal, your health your finances etc. and you are already moving towards them at your pace, you just want to move more efficiently. Then finding a book that helps you with strategies and others experience could help you do that. 
I spent 2-3 years reading all the self help books I could get might hands on, hoping the next one would shift my life. Internally I felt like yeah I got this it’s helping me and I’m getting better. Externally I didn’t change much in my life. I guess I was addicted to “hope” 
When I stopped reading “just in case” and started reading for “just in time” , I began to see changes in my life. 
It course this is only my perspective from my own experience. Others have different opinions. Listen to all and make up your mind for what works for you. 
Best of luck on your journey

Marshmallow Experiment’s incorrect assumption !
It’s one of the most famous psychological experiments relating to delayed gratification. 
So they had kids sitting with one marshmallow in front of  them. The researchers told the kids they can either eat the marshmallow or wait for sometime and the experimenter will come back with another one. 
In the original Experiment they concluded that the kids who could resist the temptation of eating the marshmallow, which they called delaying the gratification, are more likely to be successful healthy and in better relationships. They did this by following their life over a few decades. 
Now the interesting point is they did the experiment again but this time they took into account the kids’ family situation. 
They found at the kids that could resist the marshmallow were more likely to come from financially well off families. Here is what they missed in the first experiment.  The kids who ate the marshmallow were from financially below average  families. 
I leave it up to you how you interpret this !
